starting_principles: Definition of instantaneous acceleration a = dv/dt
assumptions: Acceleration a is constant over time interval [0, t]

ordered_steps.action_description: Express acceleration as first derivative of velocity
ordered_steps.justification: Definition of instantaneous rate of change of velocity.

ordered_steps.action_description: Integrate both sides with initial condition v(0) = u and final condition v(t) = v
ordered_steps.justification: Definite integration over corresponding physical limits.

ordered_steps.action_description: Factor constant acceleration out of the integral and evaluate
ordered_steps.equation_latex: [v]_{u}^{v} = a [t]_{0}^{t} \implies v - u = a t \implies v = u + a t
ordered_steps.justification: Fundamental theorem of calculus for constant integrand a.

applicability_conditions: Strictly valid only when a is independent of time t
source_references: Concepts of Physics Vol 1 by H.C. Verma (Chapter 3, p. 48)
